findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I reviewed asset-integrity.ts on its own and found no blocking defect. The exact byte hash is checked first, so older inventories that have no `skill_sha256` still need byte-exact matches. The fallback is limited to `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths that come with a well-formed 64-hex digest. The digest covers the YAML 1.2 core meaning of the header plus the exact body text after the closing delimiter, and the [metadata, body] JSON pair keeps the two parts from being confused with each other. These all fail closed by throwing rather than matching: invalid UTF-8, a missing front-matter header, YAML errors or warnings, duplicate keys, aliases, unknown tags, non-string keys, non-finite numbers, and extra documents inside the header. Changing body bytes or the meaning of metadata does change the digest. I couldn't check several things the review scope asks about because they weren't in the packet: the dispatcher/profile callers (including whether they catch the thrown errors), the inventory generator and its per-skill digest tests, the BDD/TDD discrimination, and the cleanup-marker exclusions. None of those are judged here.

Some different metadata values produce the same digest. canonicalValue converts YAML integers to JS doubles, so integers above 2^53 that differ (e.g. 9007199254740993 vs 9007199254740992) become the same value. Equivalent numeric spellings also collapse (1000, 1e3, 1000.0, 0x3E8). If a skill header were edited this way, the integrity check would still pass. Current skill front matter is mostly strings and booleans, so this is unlikely to matter in practice, and general metadata hardening is outside the accepted scope. Non-blocking.

Matching is defined by YAML 1.2 core semantics, as the doc comment says, not by how the host actually parses the file. A header rewritten from a quoted to an unquoted form that is the same in 1.2 core but different in a YAML 1.1-style parser (e.g. `"014"`→int vs `014` octal, or `"off"` vs `off`) would pass the check while the host reads a different value. The scope says not to assume the host parser is equivalent, and the risk requires someone who can already write the plugin cache. Recorded as a bounded policy note, not an error.

If the header is changed in a way that also changes the bytes between the closing `---` line and the body (e.g. a blank line added after the delimiter), the body slice changes and the check fails. That fails closed, so it is safe, but it is a false negative if desktop sync ever does this.

An empty front-matter block (`---\n---\n`) doesn't match the header regex and throws 'front matter is missing'. Shipped skills need a name and description, so this is fail-closed and not a concern for current assets.

claudeSkillSha256 and therefore claudeAssetMatches can throw TypeError, YAML parse errors, or alias ReferenceErrors instead of returning false. The packet says both production callers catch verification errors, but those callers weren't provided, so I couldn't confirm it. Either way a throw can't produce a false 'match' result.
`Array.prototype.toSorted` requires Node 20 or later. I couldn't confirm the package's engines/target from the packet.
